title: Can We Predict Before Executing Machine Learning Agents?
venue: ICLR Workshop on Lifelong Agents: Learning, Aligning, Evolving

publication.venue: ICLR Workshop on Lifelong Agents: Learning, Aligning, Evolving

mechanism.domainTask: Pre-execution pairwise preference prediction for ML-agent solutions
mechanism.populationDetail: FOREAGENT adopts AIDE's tree-search backbone, but this paper does not specify a maintained evolutionary population or enough tree state to classify it under the survey population taxonomy.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No elite archive policy is described for FOREAGENT.
mechanism.replacementDetail: AIDE tree search is inherited as a backbone; no population/archive maintenance or replacement rule is given here.
mechanism.generationDetail: AIDE proposes candidate ML solutions in parallel, but the paper does not specify a parent-child relation or variation operator.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Predicted winner and confidence gate the Top-1 candidate; actual execution then verifies it and returns trajectory feedback.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Inherited AIDE tree-search parent/node selection is not specified in this paper.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A confidence-calibrated, pre-execution pairwise solution preference model is integrated into an ML-agent search loop to gate physical verification; this is evaluation acceleration, not evolutionary search.

provenance.citationWarning: Adjacent to but outside evolutionary-search scope. Chapter 5 placement assumes foundation-model roles include the coding backbone and the separate evaluator; omit if the chapter only covers evolutionary candidate generation.
